sources.entry: Unshaky - A software attempt to address the "double key press" issue on Apple's butterfly keyboard

summary.one_liner: Unshaky is a macOS menu-bar utility that filters out accidental "double key presses" on butterfly-keyboard MacBooks by ignoring repeat keystrokes within a configurable delay.
summary.what_it_does: Unshaky addresses the double key press problem on Apple's butterfly keyboards (MacBook, MacBook Air 2018, MacBook Pro 2016 and later). It dismisses any key press that occurs within x milliseconds after the previous effective press on the same key. The delay is set per key through a "Configure" option in the menu bar icon. The README recommends starting around 40 ms and increasing gradually, and notes that some users found 60 ms or 80 ms works better. It requires Accessibility permission, and on macOS 10.15.6 and later also Input Monitoring permission. It can optionally launch at login. The README lists many user complaints about the issue and credits translators for several languages.
use_cases: fix double letters typed by a worn butterfly MacBook keyboard
ignore accidental repeated key presses on a laptop keyboard
avoid paying for a keyboard replacement on older MacBook models
configure per-key ignore delays for sticky or double-hitting keys
how_to_run: Download Unshaky.app from the README's download link
Open Unshaky and grant Accessibility permission in System Preferences -> Security & Privacy -> Privacy -> Accessibility
On macOS 10.15.6 or later, also add Unshaky.app under Privacy -> Input Monitoring
Click the Unshaky menu bar icon, choose Configure, and set a delay for the defective keys (start around 40 ms)
Optionally add Unshaky.app under System Preferences -> Users & Groups -> Login Items
notable: Per-key delay configuration from the menu bar, so only defective keys are filtered
Explains the delay tradeoff: too long a delay blocks real fast typing such as 'pp' in 'apple'
Maintenance mode: only bug fixes are planned
Localized into many languages with community translators credited
caveats: Project is in maintenance mode; only bug fixes are planned
The README says it stopped working by default on macOS 10.15.6 unless Input Monitoring is also granted (issue #166)
Only addresses the double-press symptom; it does not repair hardware
Too long a delay can block legitimate fast repeated keystrokes
